transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-27 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Oliver Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Novaris Head of Platform), Marcus Hale (Novaris Security Eng), Darya Voss (Novaris PM)

Summary: weekly pilot sync focused on governance items: SSO integration status, audit logs retention formatting, SOC2 artifacts request, data retention windows, and a short results review from pilot traffic. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: SSO/Okta flow, Audit logging granularity, Data retention policy, SOC2 evidence, Dedicated vs Hosted retention encryption, Observability/tracing for compliance

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Morales: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off — this is the Novaris pilot governance sync, we've got a fairly packed list so i'll keep it tight, priya and oliver from the eng side are here to cover SSO and logs.
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: thanks, Ethan. quick context from our side — we've been running the Redwood hosted flow with about 10k inference calls a day in the pilot, most are non-PHI but a few diagnostic flows will carry limited patient identifiers in tokenized blobs. we need to lock on retention and key ownership before we move to canary.
[00:40] Marcus Hale: yes and to reiterate from SecOps — SOC2 is table stakes, we need audit trail granularity down to request id, model version, and user id mapping, and logs retained for 365 days ideally, but we might accept 90 for the first stage. also KMS controls, i.e., customer-managed keys.
[01:05] Priya Desai: yeah we hear that — quick note, Redwood Dedicated supports KMS integrations and KMS/HSM workflows; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys but also an option for bring-your-own-key on Private. for audit logs we can stream to your S3 or to a log collector (splunk/Datadog) with events at inference start/finish and model metadata.
[01:34] Darya Voss: can you show the format of audit events? we want to map them to our SIEM fields.
[01:41] Oliver Kim: sure i'll paste the sample event in the notes after this call, but high level it's a JSON line with timestamp, request_id, model_id, model_variant, user_hash (pseudonymized), latency_ms, token_count, and a redwood_event_type. small caveat: some product names in the export might be spelled differently in transcription, but the payload is consistent.
[02:05] Marcus Hale: okay, but about pseudonymization — can you confirm we control the mapping keys? we don't want raw user ids leaving the VPC in Private.
[02:14] Priya Desai: absolutely. for Private deployments you can keep the user id mapping on-prem and only export a salted hash; for Dedicated you can choose whether to export full ids or hashed ids depending on your policy.
[02:29] Lena Ortiz: what's the retention policy config look like? is it per-route or global? we have different retention needs for embeddings vs generation logs.
[02:37] Oliver Kim: retention is per-route and per-artifact type. you can set separate windows for raw transcripts, embeddings, and aggregated metrics. default in hosted is 30 days for transcripts, 90 for emb, but we can tune that per-customer.
[02:56] Ethan Morales: quick note — Priya ran the retention simulation last night against a 2-day sample of your pilot traffic and she'll share the csv with token volumes to estimate cost and storage.
[03:07] Priya Desai: yes. attaching that — we saw about 12M tokens over two days with average per-request retention of about 240 tokens, so a 365-day window is non-trivial cost-wise. you'll see tiered estimates in the spreadsheet.
[03:29] Marcus Hale: that's helpful. we need the cost numbers tied to the retention window because budget sign-off depends on it. also, how do you support legal hold requests if we need to keep a subset longer?
[03:42] Oliver Kim: legal hold is supported via tag-based retention overrides; you can tag sessions or request IDs and Redwood will keep them for a specified longer period independent of global retention rules.
[03:55] Darya Voss: on SSO — last week's block was Okta metadata not matching, any update?
[04:02] Priya Desai: yes we resolved the metadata mismatch — there was a cert thumbprint mismatch. oliver completed a fresh metadata exchange. we had one small mapping issue where Okta group names came through as "okta_group_1" then we remapped to your internal role names.
[04:18] Lena Ortiz: cool, can you confirm the SAML assertion includes the email and groups? we need group-based RBAC mapping.
[04:24] Priya Desai: yes assertion includes email, groups, and a custom attribute for department if you push it. mapping is configurable in the console.
[04:31] Marcus Hale: is SSO tested in Dedicated or Hosted? which path are we validating?
[04:36] Ethan Morales: currently the canary is in Redwood hosted staging; plan for Dedicated staging once we hit the security gate. we proposed a final canary with Dedicated and Okta next week to validate KMS and audit log streaming.
[04:52] Darya Voss: what's the difference in audit log delivery between Hosted and Dedicated?
[04:56] Oliver Kim: Hosted streams logs to a customer-configured S3 or a forwarding endpoint; Dedicated gives you direct access to the log plane inside the tenant and you can set up an internal Fluentd sink with no egress from the subnet if you prefer. Hosted means logs transit through Redwood-managed collectors but can be forwarded encrypted to your endpoints.
[05:20] Marcus Hale: encryption-in-transit and at-rest — are you using TLS 1.2+? and keys for at-rest are AES-256?
[05:27] Priya Desai: yes TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3), at-rest is AES-256 and we support customer-managed keys via KMS for Private/Dedicated. we'll include the crypto spec in the SOC2 packet.
[05:40] Lena Ortiz: SOC2 evidence — we need the latest report and the control matrix. can you share it?
[05:45] Ethan Morales: yes, we'll attach the SOC2 type II report, the control matrix, and the bridging letter. i'll put the link in the follow-up notes. quick caveat: some artifacts are redacted for third-party secrets.
[05:58] Marcus Hale: good. also for the pilot's results — latency and error rates — we saw a couple of spikes yesterday during batch inference. what's causing that?
[06:06] Priya Desai: we looked into it — there was a misconfigured batching window that allowed a larger-than-normal window for a short period; we tightened the policy and that's reduced 95th percentile latency by about 40% in staging. we'll run that change in canary tonight.
[06:24] Lena Ortiz: do you provide token-level billing traces? our finance team wants to reconcile cost by route.
[06:30] Oliver Kim: yes per-request token accounting is in the UIs and exports. we can push a CSV to the shared drive.
[06:36] Darya Voss: on privacy — would you recommend redaction at ingestion or after model output? some of our PII is in payloads.
[06:44] Priya Desai: redaction at ingestion is safer for retention and compliance. Redwood has a preprocessor hook in Dedicated/Private where you can run redaction rules before tokens hit the model. for hosted we provide regex-based redaction and recommend you do client-side tokenization or pre-hash if possible.
[07:01] Marcus Hale: ok. can you walk through the audit log retention config UI? after the call, or briefly now?
[07:07] Oliver Kim: brief walk — in the console go to security -> audit settings, select artifact type (transcript, embedding, metric), set retention days, toggle export and choose destination. also can attach lifecycle rules for legal hold. i'll record a short screen and share the clip.
[07:23] Ethan Morales: note for the team — we'll upload a short screen recording and a sample json event.
[07:30] [silence 7s]
[07:37] Lena Ortiz: another question — compliance for EU data residency. some pilot traffic originates from EU datacenters, do you isolate storage regionally?
[07:45] Priya Desai: yes, Redwood supports region pinning. for Hosted we can pin storage and compute to AWS eu-west-1 for your account; Dedicated and Private offer more control. we'll need a formal request for residency settings so we can provision.
[07:59] Marcus Hale: what's the SLA for log availability and for data exports?
[08:05] Oliver Kim: our Dedicated SLA covers 99.95% for the control plane and 99.9% for log forwarding; for Hosted the contract provides best-effort with export guarantees we can negotiate at enterprise tier. we'll provide metrics we see in the console as part of the adoption pack.
[08:23] Darya Voss: are there any blockers from Redwood's side to enable BYOK for the pilot?
[08:28] Priya Desai: no blockers technically; for hosted we need a formal request and an onboarding window to set KMS connectivity. for Dedicated it's built in but your security team needs to approve the key rotation policy.
[08:40] Marcus Hale: audit — do you include the actual prompt text in logs? some teams want obfuscated prompts to reduce exposure.
[08:47] Oliver Kim: prompts are included by default in transcript logs for debug, but you can opt-in or turn off prompt logging. we also support hashed prompt storage where the original text is redacted and an edit distance or similarity score is stored instead.
[09:02] Lena Ortiz: excellent. what's the remediation process if something is discovered in the logs that indicates a leak?
[09:09] Priya Desai: we have an incident playbook — initial containment by disabling the affected route, rotate keys if necessary, preserve forensic snapshots to a secure bucket, and coordinate a post-mortem. we'll share the playbook doc.
[09:23] Marcus Hale: please do. also, can you confirm the frequency of compliance reviews? we want quarterly evidence dumps.
[09:29] Ethan Morales: yes quarterly reviews are standard for enterprise customers, and we can provide an ad-hoc audit at request with reasonable notice.
[09:36] Darya Voss: any surprises in the pilot's metrics we should be aware of?
[09:40] Priya Desai: the only thing was the batching misconfig which we fixed; otherwise throughput held at expected levels and model quality was stable. one note: embeddings route had higher token churn because some clients send extra context; we recommended trimming context client-side.
[09:57] Lena Ortiz: ok. one last question — do you support SAML provisioning for service accounts? we want a service principal that can only push logs to our retention bucket.
[10:06] Oliver Kim: yes service principals supported; you can issue scoped tokens with limited permissions for that purpose.
[10:11] Marcus Hale: good. next steps recap?
[10:14] Ethan Morales: recap — Redwood will: 1) share SOC2 packet and control matrix, 2) share retention simulation csv, 3) provide audit log sample json and short screen recording of UI, 4) run Okta SAML canary in Dedicated staging next week, 5) Priya to provide KMS onboarding notes. customer to confirm retention windows and share internal retention policy.
[10:36] Darya Voss: that sounds right. we'll aim to confirm retention window and share policy by Friday.
[10:41] Lena Ortiz: thanks all. happy to sign off the security gate once we have the SOC2 and the canary results look good.
[10:48] Ethan Morales: perfect. i'll follow up with the links and owners in the calendar invite. thanks everyone.
[10:55] [meeting ended]

Artifacts/links mentioned: SOC2 packet (link: https://redwood.example.com/soc2/novaris-redacted), retention simulation spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/shared/retention-novaris.csv), sample audit JSON (link: https://redwood.example.com/shared/audit-sample.json)

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mislabels of product names, filler words, and minor punctuation issues.
